name: stri_list2matrix
title: Convert a list to a character matrix

origin.description: Converts a list of atomic vectors to a character matrix.
origin.usage: stri_list2matrix(x, byrow = FALSE, fill = NA_character_, n_min = 0, by_row = byrow)

arguments.name: byrow
arguments.text: A single logical value. TRUE transposes the matrix.

arguments.name: fill
arguments.text: A single string placed where a vector runs out. The default is a missing character.

arguments.name: n_min
arguments.text: Minimum number of rows when byrow is FALSE, or of columns when byrow is TRUE.

arguments.name: by_row
arguments.text: Alias of byrow. When the caller supplies it, it replaces byrow.

origin.details: The result is always a character matrix, including when the vectors have different lengths or length 1. Every element is coerced to character. With byrow FALSE there is one column per list element: cell (i, j) is x[[j]][i], or fill past the end of that vector. The row count is the longest vector, and at least n_min. With byrow TRUE that matrix is transposed. R prints the matrix by row. as.vector walks it in column-major storage order.
origin.example:
stri_list2matrix(list(c('a', 'b'), c('c', 'd'), c('e', 'f')))
stri_list2matrix(list(c('a', 'b'), c('c', 'd'), c('e', 'f')), byrow = TRUE)
stri_list2matrix(list('a', c('b', 'c')))
stri_list2matrix(list('a', c('b', 'c')), fill = '')
stri_list2matrix(list('a', c('b', 'c')), fill = '', n_min = 5)

translation.description: Converts a list of atomic vectors to a character matrix.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A list of vectors. A string, integer, or logical value is a length-1 vector. A missing character is stringi._na.NA.

arguments.name: byrow
arguments.text: When false, each input vector becomes a column. When true, the matrix is transposed.

arguments.name: fill
arguments.text: String or NA used past the end of a short vector. The default is NA.

arguments.name: n_min
arguments.text: Minimum number of rows, or of columns when byrow is true. A negative value is an error.

arguments.name: by_row
arguments.text: When not None, replaces byrow. None leaves byrow as given.

translation.details: Returns a list of rows. Each inner list is one row from left to right, which is the order R prints. It is not R's column-major storage order. With byrow false, column j of that matrix is x[j] padded with fill, and the row count is the longest vector and at least n_min. With byrow true, that matrix is transposed, so each input vector is one row and n_min is a minimum width. A matrix with no rows is an empty list. A matrix with rows and no columns is a list of empty lists. Integers become their decimal text and logical values become TRUE or FALSE.
translation.value: A list of rows. Each inner list is one row of the character matrix.
translation.example:
from stringi._na import NA
from stringi.utils import stri_list2matrix
print(stri_list2matrix([['a', 'b'], ['c', 'd'], ['e', 'f']]))
print(stri_list2matrix([['a', 'b'], ['c', 'd'], ['e', 'f']], byrow=True))
print(stri_list2matrix(['a', ['b', 'c']]))
print(stri_list2matrix(['a', ['b', 'c']], fill=''))
print(stri_list2matrix(['a', ['b', 'c']], fill='', n_min=5))
